chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon them both) said:

I asked him about al-mubarā'ah (mutual release), how is it? He said: 'There is something due to the wife from her husband from her dowry or from something else, and he has given her part of it, and each of them dislikes the other's companion. So the wife says:

key_terms.أُبَارِئُكَ: I release you; the verbal formula used by the wife to effect the mutual release.
key_terms.الْمُبَارَاةِ: Mutual release; a form of divorce where the wife releases the husband from a debt in exchange for freedom from conjugal obligations.
key_terms.بُضْعِكِ: Your conjugal rights / your body; referring to the husband's right to sexual intimacy with the wife.
key_terms.صَدَاقِهَا: Her dowry (Mahr); the payment or property given by the husband to the wife.

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure and legal definition of Mubarā'ah in Shia Islamic family law?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam elucidates the mechanism of 'mubarā'ah', a consensual divorce where the wife forfeits her remaining dowry to secure her release, distinct from 'khul' which typically involves compensation. The narration highlights the reciprocal legal consequences: the wife's financial settlement is contingent upon the husband retaining his right to conjugal rights ('bun'uk'), a nuance emphasized by the Imams to ensure clarity in marital dissolution. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on mutual consent and precise verbal formulas to prevent future disputes over financial or physical obligations.
